body:
`$ --upload-log` (start-command 0.37.8, `src/lib/log-sanitizer.js`) removes log content that is not a secret. In one hive-mind execution log it removed 2,885,698 of 4,489,431 bytes (64%), with the same line count. The upload looks complete but the evidence is gone.

Reproduce with the shipped module:

```
printf '%s\n' \
  "gate='/tmp/hive-mind-disk-baseline-0ce9e170-e6d3-494d-91e1-0d820245d34b'" \
  '🧠 Formal AI: endpoint http://172.18.0.2:8080/api/openai/v1' \
  '{"bodyPreview":"{\"messages\":[{\"content\":\"use: curl -L -H \\\"Authorization: token $(gh auth token)\\\" -o <filename> <url>\\n...the rest of a 100 KB prompt...\"}]}"}' > sample.log
node -e 'const {sanitizeLogToTemp}=require("start-command/src/lib/log-sanitizer.js"); const r=sanitizeLogToTemp("sample.log",{env:{}}); process.stdout.write(require("fs").readFileSync(r.path,"utf8"))'
```

Output:

```
gate='/tmp/hive-mind-di[REDACTED]'
🧠 Formal AI: endpoint [REDACTED]
{"bodyPreview":"{\"messages\":[{\"content\":\"use: curl -L -H \\\"[REDACTED]
```

Three rules cause it:

1. `/(?:Proxy-)?Authorization[ \t]{0,32}:[^\r\n]*/gi` masks to the end of the line. Logged request bodies are one escaped-JSON line, and the hive-mind system prompt contains the instruction text `curl -H "Authorization: token $(gh auth token)"`. Everything after it is dropped: 26 lines, 2.9 MB in the log above. The header value has already ended at the escaped quote.
2. `/(?:https?|git|ssh):\/\/[^\s:/@]{1,256}:[^\s@]*/g` is meant for `user:password@host`, but it does not require `@`, so every URL with a port is masked: `http://172.18.0.2:8080/...` (all 202 occurrences in the log above are gone), `http://127.0.0.1:34271/session`, `http://myproxy:3128`.
3. `/(?:gh[pousr]_|github_pat_|sk-)[A-Za-z0-9_-]*/g` has no left boundary, so `disk-baseline-<uuid>` matches at `sk-`. This hits every hive-mind execution log, in the `Command:` line.

Expected:

- `Authorization:` masks only the header value: one token after an optional scheme (`Bearer`, `Basic`, `token`), stopping at whitespace, a quote, `\` or `,`. Already masked values (`[REDACTED]`) and shell expressions such as `$(gh auth token)` stay as they are.
- The URL rule matches only when `@` follows the password part: `scheme://user:pass@`.
- Token prefixes need a left boundary (`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])`).
- Regression tests with the three lines above, and the output keeps everything except the secret values.

Real logs where this happened: link-assistant/formal-ai#1364 (executions `2e56df93`, `2719fb28`). The 7 Codex execution logs in link-assistant/hive-mind#3719 differ from the originals only by rule 3.


## Affected uploads (left as published)

These 9 private gists were made with `$ --upload-log` (0.37.8) on 2026-10-23 and are linked from issues. They stay as they are. Once this issue (or #250) is fixed, the follow-up is to upload these logs again in full from the server and add the new links next to the old ones. The originals are still on the Hive Mind server in `/tmp/start-command/logs/isolation/docker/<execution>.log` (all 9 present on 2026-10-23).

comments.body: Still present on main 0.39.1 (943e4ec). link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer has the same `sk-` boundary bug (link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer#40), but handles the `Authorization` header correctly: it masks only the value and keeps the rest of the line. Moving `$ --upload-log` to that library is #250.

title: `$ --upload-log` sanitizer removes non-secret content: the Authorization rule drops the rest of the line, every URL with a port is masked, `sk-` matches inside `disk-baseline-`
